evals.prompt: Help me write a design doc for a new feature. We're building a distributed cache layer for our API to reduce database load. The API team is getting complaints about 500ms p99 latency during peak hours. We want to cache frequently accessed user profiles that don't change often. I need a complete design doc covering background, requirements, architecture, and how we'll monitor it in production.
evals.expected_output: A comprehensive markdown design document with all required sections: background/context, problem statement with metrics, functional and non-functional requirements, goals and success criteria, scope definition, high-level architecture diagram, components with responsibility boundaries, detailed low-level design with code examples for cache logic, design choices with tradeoffs, observability/metrics setup, and production readiness checklist.

assertions.name: all-11-sections-present
assertions.description: All 11 required sections must be present: Background, Problem Statement, Requirements (Func/Non-Func), Goals, Scope, HLD, Components, Design Choices, LLD, Observability, Prod Readiness

assertions.name: lld-has-code-examples
assertions.description: LLD section must contain at least 1 code block (pseudocode or actual language) showing cache implementation

assertions.name: architecture-diagram-present
assertions.description: HLD section must include ASCII art diagram, Mermaid diagram, or detailed text-based architecture visualization

assertions.name: nfr-quantified
assertions.description: NFR requirements must specify numeric targets for at least 4 metrics: latency (ms), hit rate (%), throughput (req/sec), availability (%)

assertions.name: production-readiness-complete
assertions.description: Prod Readiness section must include phased deployment strategy, canary %, rollback procedure, and pre-deployment checklist

evals.prompt: I need to document a smaller change — we're adding read replicas to our PostgreSQL database to improve query performance. It's not a brand new system, just scaling an existing one. Can you help me write a focused design doc? The current setup has one primary DB and we're adding 2 read-only replicas with async replication.
evals.expected_output: A focused design doc that skips extensive HLD (since it's a small change to existing system), but includes problem statement (current bottleneck), requirements, components affected (primary + replicas + connection pooler), detailed explanation of replication strategy, monitoring for replication lag, and production rollout plan with testing strategy.

assertions.name: hld-appropriately-brief
assertions.description: HLD section should be concise (<300 words) and not repeat full system architecture; focus only on replica topology

assertions.name: replica-configuration-detailed
assertions.description: Document must include PostgreSQL-specific configuration details: wal_level, max_wal_senders, replication slots, async streaming setup

assertions.name: replication-lag-monitoring
assertions.description: Observability section must specify how to measure replication lag and define alert threshold (e.g., >1s lag = alert)

assertions.name: failover-testing-included
assertions.description: Testing Strategy must include chaos test for promoting replica to primary and verifying read consistency

evals.prompt: We're redesigning our notification system from a simple webhook-based approach to a message queue based system (using RabbitMQ). This is a significant architectural change affecting multiple teams. Create a design document that covers everything — why we're changing, what the new architecture looks like, components and their responsibilities, how we'll migrate without breaking existing integrations, observability for the queue, and production readiness steps.
evals.expected_output: A comprehensive design doc with full depth: background on current limitations, problem statement with impact metrics, detailed requirements (functional like message durability/ordering, non-functional like throughput), clear scope including what's NOT changing, HLD with diagrams showing webhook system vs new queue-based system, detailed component breakdown (producer, queue, consumer, retry logic), LLD with code examples for publishing/consuming messages, migration/compatibility strategy, observability metrics and alerts, disaster recovery plan, and deployment phases.

assertions.name: webhook-vs-queue-comparison
assertions.description: Document must contain explicit comparison of webhook vs message queue approaches with at least 5 comparison points

assertions.name: producer-consumer-code
assertions.description: LLD section must include at least 2 code blocks: one showing message producer implementation, one showing consumer implementation

assertions.name: backward-compatibility-strategy
assertions.description: Document must explain how existing webhook integrations continue working during migration (adapter pattern, dual-write, etc.) with specific phased migration plan including % traffic targets

assertions.name: queue-observability-metrics
assertions.description: Observability section must specify metrics: queue_depth, processing_lag_ms, dlq_size with defined alert thresholds

assertions.name: disaster-recovery-plan
assertions.description: Prod Readiness must include message retention policy, dead-letter queue strategy, RTO/RPO targets, and failure scenario playbooks
